title.zh: 卷二百六十四 列傳第二十三 薛居正 沈倫 盧多遜 宋琪 宋雄
title.en: Volume 264 Biographies 23: Xue Juzheng, Shen Lun, Lu Duoxun, Song Qi, Song Xiong
title.raw: 卷二百六十四 列傳第二十三 薛居正 沈倫 盧多遜 宋琪 宋雄 Volume 264 Biographies 23: Xue Juzheng, Shen Lun, Lu Duoxun, Song Qi, Song Xiong

sentences.zh: 薛居正

translations.literal: Xue Juzheng
translations.idiomatic: Xue Juzheng

sentences.zh: 薛居正，字子平，開封浚儀人。

translations.literal: Xue Juzheng, courtesy name Ziping, was a man of Junyi in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Juzheng, courtesy name Ziping, was a native of Junyi in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父仁謙，周太子賓客。

translations.literal: His father Renqian was a guest of the crown prince under the Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Renqian had served as a guest of the crown prince under the Later Zhou.

sentences.zh: 居正少好學，有大志。

translations.literal: Juzheng in youth loved learning and had great aspirations.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Juzheng loved learning and cherished lofty ambitions.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，舉進士不第，為《遣愁文》以自解，寓意倜儻，識者以為有公輔之量。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he presented himself for the jinshi examination but failed; he wrote an "Essay to Dispel Melancholy" to console himself. Its meaning was free and unconventional, and those who knew him regarded him as having the measure of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qingtai era he failed the jinshi examination and wrote an "Essay to Dispel Melancholy" to console himself. Its spirit was bold and unconventional, and those who knew him took this as a sign that he had the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 逾年，登第。

translations.literal: The next year he passed the examination.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he passed the examination.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，華帥劉遂凝辟為從事。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin, the military governor of Hua, Liu Suing, recruited him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu era of the Later Jin, Liu Suing, military governor of Hua, recruited him as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 遂凝兄遂清領邦計，奏署鹽鐵巡官。

translations.literal: Suing's elder brother Suiqing oversaw the state's fiscal administration and memorialized to appoint him salt-and-iron patrol officer.
translations.idiomatic: Suing's elder brother Suiqing, who oversaw state finances, had him appointed salt-and-iron patrol officer on memorial.

sentences.zh: 開運初，改度支推官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun he was transferred to revenue-section investigator.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kaiyun era he was transferred to investigator in the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 宰相李崧領鹽鐵，又奏署推官，加大理寺直，遷右拾遺。

translations.literal: The chief minister Li Song oversaw salt and iron; he again memorialized to appoint him investigator, with promotion to direct clerk of the Court of Judicial Review, then transfer to right remonstrance-reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Song, who also oversaw salt and iron affairs, again had him appointed investigator and promoted to direct clerk of the Court of Judicial Review, then transferred him to the post of right remonstrance-reminder.

sentences.zh: 桑維翰為開封府尹，奏署判官。

translations.literal: Sang Weihan was prefect of Kaifeng; he memorialized to appoint him judge.
translations.idiomatic: When Sang Weihan became prefect of Kaifeng, he had Juzheng appointed as a judicial officer in the prefectural administration.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐初，史弘肇領侍衛親軍，威權震主，殘忍自恣，無敢忤其意者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou under Han, Shi Hongzhao commanded the personal guard army; his authority shook the ruler, he was cruel and willful, and none dared oppose his will.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qianyou era of the Later Han, Shi Hongzhao commanded the personal guard army. His power overshadowed the throne, he was cruel and arbitrary, and no one dared defy him.

sentences.zh: 其部下吏告民犯鹽禁，法當死。

translations.literal: A subordinate clerk under him reported that a commoner had violated the salt prohibition; by law he should die.
translations.idiomatic: One of his subordinate clerks reported that a commoner had violated the salt monopoly; the penalty was death.

sentences.zh: 獄將決，居正疑其不實，召詰之，乃吏與民有私憾，因誣之，逮吏鞫之，具伏抵法。

translations.literal: As the case was about to be decided, Juzheng doubted that it was true; he summoned and questioned the man, and it turned out the clerk and the commoner had a private grudge and the clerk had framed him. He arrested the clerk and interrogated him; the clerk fully confessed and was punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was about to be decided, Juzheng suspected the charge was false. He summoned the accused and questioned him, learning that the clerk bore a private grudge and had framed him. Juzheng arrested the clerk, interrogated him until he confessed fully, and had him punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 弘肇雖怒甚，亦無以屈。

translations.literal: Although Hongzhao was very angry, he had no means to bend Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Though Hongzhao was furious, he could not make Juzheng yield.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，遷比部員外郎，領三司推官，旋知制誥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun under Zhou he was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Revenue, concurrently head investigator of the Three Departments, and soon after was made drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Guangshun era of the Later Zhou he was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue, served concurrently as chief investigator of the Three Departments, and soon became a drafter of imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 周祖征兗州，詔居正從行，以勞加都官郎中。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder campaigned against Yanzhou, he was ordered to accompany the expedition; for his service he was promoted to director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder campaigned against Yanzhou, Juzheng was ordered to accompany him and, for his service, was promoted to director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 顯德三年，遷左諫議大夫，擢弘文館學士，判館事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiande he was transferred to left remonstrance and policy adviser, promoted to academician of the Hongwen Hall, and given charge of the hall's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiande he was made left remonstrance and policy adviser, appointed academician of the Hongwen Hall, and placed in charge of its affairs.

sentences.zh: 六年，使滄州定民租。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was sent to Cangzhou to fix the people's land tax.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was dispatched to Cangzhou to fix the people's land tax assessments.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以材幹聞於朝，擢刑部侍郎，判吏部銓。

translations.literal: Before long, for his talent and capacity he became known at court; he was promoted to vice minister of justice and given charge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection board.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his ability became known at court, and he was promoted to vice minister of justice with concurrent charge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection board.

sentences.zh: 宋初，遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was transferred to vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song he was promoted to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 太祖親征李筠及李重進，並判留司三司，俄出知許州。

translations.literal: When Taizu personally campaigned against Li Jin and Li Chongjin, Juzheng concurrently judged the Three Departments left at the capital; soon after he went out to serve as prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu personally campaigned against Li Jin and Li Chongjin, Juzheng was left in charge of the Three Departments at the capital; soon afterward he was sent out as prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，入為樞密直學士，權知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong he entered the capital as academician directly attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs and was given provisional charge of the civil-service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianlong he returned to the capital as academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and was given provisional charge of the civil-service examinations.

sentences.zh: 初平湖湘，以居正知朗州。

translations.literal: When the lake and Xiang region were first pacified, Juzheng was made prefect of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the lake and Xiang region were first pacified, Juzheng was appointed prefect of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 會亡卒數千人聚山澤為盜，監軍使疑城中僧千餘人皆其黨，議欲盡捕誅之。

translations.literal: It happened that several thousand discharged soldiers gathered in mountains and marshes as bandits; the military supervisor suspected that more than a thousand monks in the city were all their accomplices and proposed to arrest and execute them all.
translations.idiomatic: At the time several thousand discharged soldiers had gathered in the hills and marshes as bandits. The military supervisor suspected that more than a thousand monks in the city were all their accomplices and proposed arresting and executing every one of them.

sentences.zh: 居正以計緩其事，因率眾剪滅群寇，擒賊帥汪端，詰之，僧皆不預，賴以全活。

translations.literal: Juzheng by stratagem delayed the matter, then led troops to cut down and destroy the bandit bands, captured the bandit chief Wang Duan, and questioned him; the monks had all taken no part, and thanks to this they were preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng used a stratagem to delay the massacre, then led troops to destroy the bandit bands, captured their leader Wang Duan, and questioned him. The monks had taken no part, and so they were spared.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，加兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande he was given the additional title of vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qiande era he was promoted to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 車駕將親征太原，大發民饋運。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage was about to campaign personally against Taiyuan, and the people were mobilized on a great scale to transport provisions.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor was about to campaign personally against Taiyuan, the people were mobilized on a vast scale to transport supplies.

sentences.zh: 時河南府饑，逃亡者四萬家，上憂之，命居正馳傳招集，浹旬間民盡復業。

translations.literal: At the time Henan prefecture suffered famine and forty thousand households had fled; the emperor was troubled and ordered Juzheng to travel post-haste to summon them back; within ten days the people had all returned to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Henan prefecture was then suffering famine, and forty thousand households had fled. The emperor was troubled and ordered Juzheng to travel post-haste to summon them back; within ten days the people had all returned to their occupations.

sentences.zh: 以本官參知政事。

translations.literal: With his existing office he became participant in governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed participant in governance while retaining his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 五年，加吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was given the additional title of vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was given the additional title of vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 開寶五年，兼淮南、湖南、嶺南等道都提舉三司水陸發運使事，又兼判門下侍郎，監修國史；

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaibao he concurrently held overall charge of the Three Departments' water-and-land transport commissioners for Huainan, Hunan, Lingnan, and other circuits; he also concurrently judged the vice director of the Chancellery and supervised the compilation of the national history;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaibao he was given overall charge of water-and-land transport for Huainan, Hunan, Lingnan, and other circuits, and concurrently served as vice director of the Chancellery and supervisor of the national history;

sentences.zh: 又監修《五代史》，逾年畢，錫以器幣。

translations.literal: he also supervised the compilation of the History of the Five Dynasties; after more than a year it was completed, and he was rewarded with vessels and silks.
translations.idiomatic: he also supervised compilation of the History of the Five Dynasties. When it was finished the following year, he was rewarded with ritual vessels and silks.

sentences.zh: 六年，拜門下侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed vice director of the Chancellery and grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed vice director of the Chancellery and grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 八年二月，上謂居正等曰：“年穀方登，庶物豐盛，若非上天垂祐，何以及斯。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year the emperor said to Juzheng and the others: "The year's grain has just been harvested and all things are abundant; if not for Heaven's gracious protection, how could we have reached this."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year the emperor said to Juzheng and the others, "The harvest has just been gathered in and all things are abundant. Had Heaven not shown its favor, how could we have reached this point?

sentences.zh: 所宜共思濟物，或有闕政，當與振舉，以成朕志。

translations.literal: "You should jointly think of benefiting the people; if there are any defects in government, you should raise and rectify them to fulfill my intent."
translations.idiomatic: You should together consider how to benefit the people. Where government falls short, you should raise and remedy it to fulfill my intent."

sentences.zh: ”居正等益修政事，以副上意焉。

translations.literal: Juzheng and the others thereupon further cultivated government affairs to accord with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng and the others thereupon redoubled their efforts in government to meet the emperor's wishes.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，加左僕射、昭文館大學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was given the additional titles of left vice director and grand academician of the Zhaowen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was promoted to left vice director and grand academician of the Zhaowen Hall.

sentences.zh: 從平晉陽還，進位司空。

translations.literal: Returning from the pacification of Jinyang, he was advanced to the rank of minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from the pacification of Jinyang, he was advanced to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 因服丹砂遇毒，方奏事，覺疾作，遽出。

translations.literal: Because he took cinnabar and encountered poison, while he was presenting business he felt illness come on and hurried out.
translations.idiomatic: Having taken cinnabar and suffered poisoning, he was in the middle of presenting business when he felt illness strike and hurried out.

sentences.zh: 至殿門外，飲水升餘，堂吏掖歸中書，已不能言，但指廡間儲水器。

translations.literal: Reaching outside the hall gate he drank more than a sheng of water; a hall clerk supported him back to the Secretariat, but he could no longer speak and only pointed to the water vessels stored in the corridor.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the outer hall gate he drank more than a sheng of water. A clerk of the hall supported him back to the Secretariat, but he could no longer speak and only pointed to the water vessels stored in the corridor.

sentences.zh: 左右取水至，不能飲，偃閣中，吐氣如煙焰，輿歸私第卒，六年六月也，年七十。

translations.literal: Attendants brought water, but he could not drink; he lay prostrate in the pavilion, his exhaled breath like smoke and flame; he was carried in a litter to his private residence and died—it was the sixth month of the sixth year, at age seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants brought water, but he could not drink. He collapsed in the pavilion, his breath rising like smoke and flame. He was carried home in a litter and died there in the sixth month of the sixth year, at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉、中書令，諡文惠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the titles of grand marshal and director of the Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wenhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as grand marshal and director of the Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wenhui.

sentences.zh: 居正氣貌瑰偉，飲酒至數斗不亂。

translations.literal: Juzheng's bearing and appearance were magnificent and imposing; he could drink several dou of wine without disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng had a magnificent and imposing presence and could drink several dou of wine without losing his composure.

sentences.zh: 性孝行純，居家儉約。

translations.literal: By nature he was filial and pure in conduct, and at home he was frugal.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was filial and upright in conduct, and he lived frugally at home.

sentences.zh: 為相任寬簡，不好苛察，士君子以此多之。

translations.literal: As chief minister he was lenient and simple, disliking harsh scrutiny, and gentlemen for this reason greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister he was lenient and unpretentious and disliked harsh scrutiny; for this the gentry greatly esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 自參政至為相，凡十八年，恩遇始終不替。

translations.literal: From participant in governance to chief minister, altogether eighteen years—favor and treatment from beginning to end never declined.
translations.idiomatic: From his appointment as participant in governance until his death as chief minister, a span of eighteen years, imperial favor toward him never waned.

sentences.zh: 先是，太祖嘗謂居正曰：“自古為君者鮮克正己，為臣者多無遠略，雖居顯位，不能垂名後代，而身陷不義，子孫罹殃，蓋君臣之道有所未盡。

translations.literal: Earlier Taizu had once said to Juzheng: "From antiquity rulers have rarely been able to correct themselves, and ministers for the most part lack far-reaching plans; though they occupy eminent positions they cannot leave their names to later generations, yet fall into unrighteousness and their descendants suffer calamity—this is because the way between ruler and minister has in some measure not been fully carried out."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Taizu had once told Juzheng, "Since antiquity few rulers have been able to correct themselves, and most ministers lack far-reaching vision. Though they hold high office, they cannot leave their names to posterity, yet fall into unrighteousness and bring calamity on their descendants—because the bond between ruler and minister has not been fully honored.

sentences.zh: 吾觀唐太宗受人諫疏，直詆其非而不恥。

translations.literal: "I observe that Emperor Taizong of Tang received remonstrance memorials from others and, though they directly denounced his faults, was not ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: I see that Emperor Taizong of Tang accepted remonstrance memorials that directly denounced his faults without shame.

sentences.zh: 以朕所見，不若自不為之，使人無異詞。

translations.literal: "As I see it, it is better simply not to do wrong, so that people have no differing words."
translations.idiomatic: As I see it, it is better simply not to do wrong in the first place, so that no one has cause to speak against you.

sentences.zh: 又觀古之人臣多不終始，能保全而享厚福者，由忠正也。

translations.literal: "Again I observe that ancient ministers for the most part did not see things through from beginning to end; those who could preserve themselves and enjoy thick blessings did so through loyalty and rectitude."
translations.idiomatic: I also observe that most ministers of old did not see things through to the end; those who preserved themselves and enjoyed lasting good fortune did so through loyalty and rectitude."

sentences.zh: ”開寶中，居正與沈倫並為相，盧多遜參知政事，九年冬，多遜亦為平章事。

translations.literal: In the Kaibao era Juzheng and Shen Lun were both chief ministers; Lu Duoxun was participant in governance; in the winter of the ninth year Duoxun also became grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era Juzheng and Shen Lun served together as chief ministers while Lu Duoxun was participant in governance; in the winter of the ninth year Duoxun also became grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 及居正卒，而沈倫責授，多遜南流，論者以居正守道蒙福，果符太祖之言。

translations.literal: When Juzheng died, Shen Lun was demoted by assignment and Duoxun was banished south; commentators held that Juzheng, by keeping to the Way, received blessing—truly matching Taizu's words.
translations.idiomatic: When Juzheng died, Shen Lun was demoted by reassignment and Duoxun was banished to the south. Commentators held that Juzheng, by keeping to the Way, had received its reward—exactly as Taizu had foretold.

sentences.zh: 居正好讀書，為文落筆不能自休。

translations.literal: Juzheng loved reading books; when he wrote, his brush could not stop of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng loved reading, and when he wrote his brush would not stop of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 子惟吉集為三十卷上之，賜名《文惠集》。

translations.literal: His son Weiji collected his works into thirty juan and presented them; the collection was granted the name Collected Works of Wenhui.
translations.idiomatic: His son Weiji collected his writings into thirty juan and presented them to the throne, which granted the collection the title Collected Works of Wenhui.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，詔以居正配饗太祖廟庭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping an edict ordered that Juzheng be given paired sacrifice in Taizu's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping an edict ordered that Juzheng receive paired sacrifice in Taizu's temple court.

sentences.zh: 子 惟吉

translations.literal: Son: Weiji
translations.idiomatic: Son: Weiji

sentences.zh: 惟吉，字世康，居正假子也。

translations.literal: Weiji, courtesy name Shikang, was Juzheng's adopted son.
translations.idiomatic: Weiji, courtesy name Shikang, was Juzheng's adopted son.

sentences.zh: 居正妻妒悍，無子，婢妾皆不得侍側，故養惟吉，愛之甚篤。

translations.literal: Juzheng's wife was jealous and fierce; she had no sons, and maidservants and concubines were all forbidden to attend at her side; therefore he raised Weiji and loved him with utmost devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng's wife was jealous and overbearing. She bore no sons and would not allow maidservants or concubines near her husband, so he adopted Weiji and loved him devotedly.

sentences.zh: 少有勇力，形質魁岸，與京師少年追逐，角抵蹴踘，縱酒不謹。

translations.literal: In youth he had courage and strength; his form and stature were towering; he ran with the young men of the capital, wrestling and playing cuju, drinking recklessly without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was strong and bold, with a towering build. He ran with the young men of the capital, wrestling and playing cuju, and drank without restraint.

sentences.zh: 雅好音樂，嘗與伶人遊，居正不能知。

translations.literal: He was by nature fond of music and once associated with actors; Juzheng did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of music and once kept company with actors, of which Juzheng remained unaware.

sentences.zh: 蔭補右千牛衛備身，歷太子通奉舍人，改西頭供奉官。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he was appointed attendant of the Right Palace Guard; he served as attendant for presentation to the crown prince, then was transferred to attendant of the western headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: By hereditary privilege he was appointed attendant of the Right Palace Guard, served as attendant for presentation to the crown prince, and was later transferred to attendant of the western headquarters.

sentences.zh: 淳化五年，秦州溫仲舒以伐木為蕃戶攘奪，驅其部落徙居渭北，頗致騷動。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunhua, Wen Zhongshu of Qinzhou, because logging led to seizure by Tangut households, drove their tribes to relocate north of the Wei River, causing considerable unrest.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chunhua, Wen Zhongshu of Qinzhou, whose logging had provoked raids by Tangut households, drove their tribes to relocate north of the Wei River, causing considerable unrest.

sentences.zh: 詔擇守臣安撫之，乃命惟吉與仲舒對易其任。

translations.literal: An edict ordered selection of a guarding minister to pacify them; thereupon Weiji was ordered to exchange posts with Zhongshu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that a suitable frontier official be chosen to pacify the region, and Weiji was appointed to exchange posts with Zhongshu.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷左領軍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to great general of the Left Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to great general of the Left Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，移知延州，未行，卒，年四十二。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao he was transferred to serve as prefect of Yanzhou; before he set out he died, at age forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhidao he was appointed prefect of Yanzhou, but died before taking up the post, at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 惟吉既知非改過，能折節下士，輕財好施，所至有能聲。

translations.literal: Once Weiji knew his faults and reformed, he could humble himself before scholars, was light with wealth and fond of giving, and wherever he went had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Once he recognized his faults and reformed, Weiji could humble himself before scholars, was generous with wealth, and wherever he served earned a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 然御家無法，及其死，家人爭財致訟，妻子辨對於公庭云。

translations.literal: Yet he had no method in governing his household; when he died his family members fought over property and brought lawsuits, and wife and children argued their cases in the public court.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had no discipline in managing his household. After his death his family fought over his property in lawsuits, and wife and children argued their cases in open court.

sentences.zh: 沈倫，字順儀，開封太康人。

translations.literal: Shen Lun, courtesy name Shunyi, was a man of Taikang in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Lun, courtesy name Shunyi, was a native of Taikang in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 舊名義倫，以與太宗名下字同，止名倫。

translations.literal: His former name was Yilun; because it shared a character with Taizong's taboo name, he was called only Lun.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Yilun; because it shared a character with Taizong's taboo name, he was called only Lun.

sentences.zh: 少習《三禮》於嵩、洛間，以講學自給。

translations.literal: In youth he studied the Three Rites between Song and Luo and supported himself by lecturing.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied the Three Rites in the Song and Luo region and supported himself by teaching.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，白文珂鎮陝，倫往依之。

translations.literal: In the Qianyou era under Han, Bai Wenke governed Shaan, and Lun went to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyou era of the Later Han, when Bai Wenke governed Shaan, Lun went to serve under him.

sentences.zh: 周顯德初，太祖領同州節度，宣徽使昝居潤與倫厚善，薦於太祖，留幕府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande under Zhou, Taizu held the Tongzhou command; the palace commissioner Zan Jurun was on close terms with Lun and recommended him to Taizu, who retained him in the headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Xiande era, when Taizu held the Tongzhou command, Palace Commissioner Zan Jurun, who was on close terms with Lun, recommended him to Taizu, who retained him on his staff.

sentences.zh: 太祖繼領滑、許、宋三鎮，皆署從事，掌留後財貨，以廉聞。

translations.literal: Taizu successively held the three commands of Hua, Xu, and Song; in each Lun was appointed staff officer in charge of the regent's finances, and he became known for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu successively held the commands of Hua, Xu, and Song, Lun served on his staff in each, managing the regent's finances, and became known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 及受周禪，自宋州觀察推官召為戶部郎中。

translations.literal: When he received the Zhou abdication, Lun was summoned from investigating officer of Song prefecture to director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu received the Zhou abdication, Lun was summoned from investigating officer of Song prefecture to director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 奉使吳越歸，奏便宜十數事，皆從之。

translations.literal: Returning from a mission to Wuyue, he memorialized more than ten items of timely advantage, and all were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from a mission to Wuyue, he memorialized more than a dozen practical proposals, all of which were adopted.

sentences.zh: 道出揚、泗，屬歲饑，民多死，郡長吏白於倫曰：“郡中軍儲尚百餘萬斛，倘貸於民，至秋復收新粟，如此則公私俱利，非公言不可。

translations.literal: Passing through Yang and Si, it happened to be a year of famine and many of the people died; the chief officials of the commandery reported to Lun: "Military stores in the commandery still exceed a million hu; if we lend to the people and in autumn collect the new grain again, thus both public and private will benefit—it cannot be done without your words."
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Yang and Si, he found famine abroad and many dead. The chief officials of the commandery told him, "Military stores in the commandery still exceed a million hu. If we lend grain to the people and collect the new harvest in autumn, both public and private interests will be served. This cannot be done without your support.

sentences.zh: ”還具以白。

translations.literal: On his return he fully reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: "On his return he reported the proposal fully to the throne.

sentences.zh: 朝論沮之曰：“今以軍儲振饑民，若薦饑無徵，孰任其咎？

translations.literal: Court discussion obstructed it, saying: "Now if we use military stores to relieve starving people, and if famine returns year after year with no collection, who will bear the blame?"
translations.idiomatic: Court discussion opposed it, saying, "If we use military stores to relieve the starving and famine returns year after year with no repayment, who will bear the blame?

sentences.zh: ”太祖以問，倫曰：“國家以廩粟濟民，自當召和氣，致豐稔，豈復有水旱耶？

translations.literal: Taizu asked Lun, who said: "When the state uses granary grain to aid the people, it should naturally summon harmonious qi and bring abundant harvest—how could there again be flood and drought?"
translations.idiomatic: "Taizu asked Lun, who replied, "When the state uses granary grain to aid the people, it should naturally summon harmonious qi and bring abundant harvests. How could flood and drought return?

sentences.zh: 此當決於宸衷。

translations.literal: "This should be decided in the imperial heart."
translations.idiomatic: This should be decided by Your Majesty's own judgment."

sentences.zh: ”太祖即命發廩貸民。

translations.literal: Taizu at once ordered the granaries opened to lend to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu at once ordered the granaries opened to lend grain to the people.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，遷給事中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong he was transferred to attendant within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianlong he was promoted to attendant within the palace.

sentences.zh: 明年春，為陝西轉運使。

translations.literal: The next spring he became transport commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he was appointed transport commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 王師伐蜀，用為隨軍水陸轉運使。

translations.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Shu, he was used as water-and-land transport commissioner accompanying the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army campaigned against Shu, he was appointed water-and-land transport commissioner accompanying the army.

sentences.zh: 先是，王全斌、崔彥進之入成都也，競取民家玉帛子女，倫獨居佛寺疏食，有以珍異奇巧物為獻者，倫皆拒之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Quanbin and Cui Yanjin entered Chengdu, they competed to seize jade, silks, and daughters from the people's households; Lun alone dwelt in a Buddhist temple on plain food, and when people presented rare, exotic, or ingenious objects, Lun refused them all.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wang Quanbin and Cui Yanjin entered Chengdu, they competed to seize jade, silks, and women from the populace. Lun alone lived in a Buddhist temple on plain food, and when people offered him rare or ingenious treasures, he refused them all.

sentences.zh: 東歸，篋中所有，才圖書數卷而已。

translations.literal: Returning east, all he had in his case was only several rolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: Returning east, all he carried in his baggage were a few rolls of books.

sentences.zh: 太祖知之，遂貶全斌等，以倫為戶部侍郎、樞密副使。

translations.literal: Taizu learned of this, thereupon demoted Quanbin and the others, and made Lun vice minister of revenue and vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu learned of this, he demoted Quanbin and the others and appointed Lun vice minister of revenue and vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 親征太原，領大內都部署、判留司三司事。

translations.literal: On the personal campaign against Taiyuan he headed overall deployment of the inner palace and judged the Three Departments left at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Taiyuan he was left in overall charge of the inner palace and the Three Departments at the capital.

sentences.zh: 先是，倫第庳陋，處之晏如。

translations.literal: Earlier Lun's residence was low and shabby; he dwelt in it with perfect ease.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Lun's house had been low and shabby, yet he lived in it with perfect ease.

sentences.zh: 時權要多冒禁市巨木秦、隴間，以營私宅，及事敗露，皆自啟於上前。

translations.literal: At the time many in power illicitly purchased huge timber in the Qin and Long region in violation of prohibitions to build private residences; when the matter was exposed they all reported themselves before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many powerful officials had illicitly purchased huge timber in the Qin and Long region to build private residences. When the matter was exposed, they all reported themselves to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 倫亦嘗為母市木營佛舍，因奏其事。

translations.literal: Lun too had once purchased timber for his mother to build a Buddhist chapel and thereupon memorialized the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Lun too had once purchased timber for his mother to build a Buddhist chapel and memorialized the matter himself.

sentences.zh: 太祖笑謂曰：“爾非逾矩者。

translations.literal: Taizu smiled and said to him: "You are not one who oversteps bounds."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu smiled and said, "You are not one who oversteps the bounds.

sentences.zh: ”知其未葺居第，因遣中使按圖督工為治之。

translations.literal: Knowing that he had not yet built a dwelling, Taizu thereupon sent a palace envoy according to a plan to supervise workers in constructing one for him.
translations.idiomatic: "Knowing that he had not yet built a proper residence, Taizu sent a palace envoy with plans to supervise construction of one for him.

sentences.zh: 倫私告使者，願得制度狹小，使者以聞，上亦不違其志。

translations.literal: Lun privately told the envoy that he wished the scale to be narrow and small; the envoy reported this, and the emperor also did not go against his wish.
translations.idiomatic: Lun privately asked the envoy to keep the house small and modest. When the envoy reported this, the emperor did not go against his wish.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，丁母憂，起復視事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he entered mourning for his mother and was recalled from mourning to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao he entered mourning for his mother and was recalled from mourning to resume office.

sentences.zh: 六年，拜中書侍郎、平章事、集賢殿大學士兼提舉荊南、劍南水陸發運事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat, grand councilor, and grand academician of the Jixian Hall, concurrently overseeing water-and-land transport for Jingnan and Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat, grand councilor, and grand academician of the Jixian Hall, with concurrent charge of water-and-land transport for Jingnan and Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 雩祀西洛，以倫留守東京兼大內都部署。

translations.literal: For the rain prayer sacrifice in western Luo, Lun was left to guard the eastern capital and concurrently head overall deployment of the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor performed the rain-prayer sacrifice in western Luo, Lun was left to guard the eastern capital with overall charge of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 俄召赴行在，令預大禮。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to the traveling palace and ordered to take part in the great ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was summoned to the traveling palace to take part in the great ceremony.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，加右僕射兼門下侍郎，監修國史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was given the additional titles of right vice director and concurrent vice director of the Chancellery, and supervised the national history.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was promoted to right vice director with concurrent appointment as vice director of the Chancellery and supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 親征太原，復以倫為留守、判開封府事。

translations.literal: On the personal campaign against Taiyuan, Lun was again made regent and judge of Kaifeng prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Taiyuan he was again left as regent and placed in charge of Kaifeng prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 師還，加左僕射。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was given the additional title of left vice director.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was promoted to left vice director.

sentences.zh: 五年，史官李昉、扈蒙撰《太祖實錄》五十卷，倫為監修以獻，賜襲衣、金帶。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the historiographers Li Fang and Hu Meng compiled fifty juan of the Veritable Records of Taizu; Lun supervised the compilation and presented it, and was rewarded with ceremonial robes and a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the historiographers Li Fang and Hu Meng compiled fifty juan of the Veritable Records of Taizu. Lun supervised the work and presented it to the throne, receiving ceremonial robes and a gold belt in reward.

sentences.zh: 六年，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was given the additional title of commissioner with the ceremony of three excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was given the honorary rank of commissioner with the ceremony of the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 是歲疾作，自是多請告。

translations.literal: That year illness came on him, and from then on he often requested leave.
translations.idiomatic: That year he fell ill and thereafter often requested leave from office.

sentences.zh: 盧多遜事將發，倫已上表求致仕。

translations.literal: When Lu Duoxun's affair was about to break, Lun had already submitted a memorial requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Duoxun's affair was about to break, Lun had already submitted a memorial requesting retirement.

sentences.zh: 明年多遜敗，以倫與之同列，不能覺察，詔加切責，降授工部尚書。

translations.literal: The next year Duoxun was ruined; because Lun had been his colleague and had not detected it, an edict sharply rebuked him and demoted him by appointment to minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when Duoxun fell, Lun was sharply rebuked by edict for having served as his colleague without detecting his conduct, and was demoted to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 其子都官員外郎繼宗，本由父蔭，不宜更在朝行，可落班簿。

translations.literal: His son Jizong, vice director in the Ministry of Justice, had originally entered office by his father's privilege; he should not remain in the court ranks and was removed from the roster.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jizong, vice director in the Ministry of Justice, had entered office through his father's privilege and was removed from the court roster.

sentences.zh: 時倫病不能興，上表謝。

translations.literal: At the time Lun was ill and could not rise; he submitted a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was then too ill to rise and submitted a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 未幾，倫再奉章乞骸骨，復授左僕射致仕。

translations.literal: Before long Lun again submitted a memorial begging to retire on old bones, and was again granted left vice director with retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Lun again petitioned to retire, and was restored to the rank of left vice director with permission to retire.

sentences.zh: 上以倫國初舊臣，遽復繼宗官以慰其心。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Lun was an old minister from the founding of the state, quickly restored Jizong's office to comfort his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Because Lun was an old minister from the founding of the dynasty, the emperor quickly restored Jizong's office to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年，卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi he died, at age seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongxi he died at the age of seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 倫清介醇謹，車駕每出，多令居守。

translations.literal: Lun was pure, upright, sincere, and cautious; whenever the imperial carriage went out, he was often ordered to remain on guard.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was pure, upright, and scrupulously cautious. Whenever the emperor traveled, Lun was usually left to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 好釋氏，信因果。

translations.literal: He favored Buddhism and believed in cause and effect.
translations.idiomatic: He favored Buddhism and believed in karmic retribution.

sentences.zh: 嘗盛夏坐室中，恣蚊蚋噆其膚，童子秉箑至，輒叱之，冀以徼福。

translations.literal: Once in midsummer he sat in his room and let mosquitoes and gnats bite his skin at will; when a boy came bearing a fan he always scolded him away, hoping thereby to seek merit.
translations.idiomatic: Once in midsummer he sat in his room and let mosquitoes bite his skin freely. When a boy came with a fan he always scolded him away, hoping thereby to gain merit.

sentences.zh: 在相位日，值歲饑，鄉人假粟者皆與之，殆至千斛，歲餘盡焚其券。

translations.literal: While he was chief minister, when famine struck he gave grain to all fellow townsmen who borrowed it, nearly reaching a thousand hu; after more than a year he burned all their IOUs.
translations.idiomatic: While he served as chief minister, during a famine he lent grain to fellow townsmen who asked, nearly a thousand hu in all. More than a year later he burned all their IOUs.

sentences.zh: 微時娶閻氏，無子，妾田氏生繼宗。

translations.literal: In humble days he married the Yan clan; she had no sons, and the concubine of the Tian clan bore Jizong.
translations.idiomatic: In his early days he married a woman of the Yan clan, who bore no sons. His concubine of the Tian clan bore Jizong.

sentences.zh: 及貴，閻以封邑固讓田，倫乃為閻治第太康，田遂為正室，搢紳非之。

translations.literal: When he became eminent, Yan firmly yielded her fief to Tian; Lun thereupon built a residence for Yan in Taikang, and Tian then became the principal wife—gentlemen disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: When he rose to high office, Yan firmly yielded her noble fief to Tian. Lun built a residence for Yan in Taikang, and Tian became his principal wife—a move the gentry disapproved.

sentences.zh: 初，有司議諡倫曰恭惠，繼宗上言曰：“亡父始從冠歲，即事儒業，未遑從賊，遽赴賓招，叨遇明時，陟於相位。

translations.literal: Earlier the relevant offices proposed the posthumous name Gonghui for Lun; Jizong submitted a statement saying: "My late father from the age of capping devoted himself to Confucian studies, had no leisure to follow bandits, and promptly answered an invitation to office; he undeservedly met a bright age and rose to the rank of chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the relevant offices had proposed the posthumous name Gonghui for Lun. Jizong submitted a statement saying, "My late father from youth devoted himself to Confucian studies, never had leisure to follow rebels, and promptly answered the call to office. He undeservedly met a bright age and rose to chief minister.

sentences.zh: 伏見國朝故相，薛居正諡‘文惠’，王溥諡‘文獻’，此雖近制，實為典常。

translations.literal: "I humbly observe that former chief ministers of our dynasty, Xue Juzheng with posthumous name Wenhui and Wang Pu with posthumous name Wenxian—though this is recent precedent, it is in truth established custom."
translations.idiomatic: I observe that former chief ministers of our dynasty, Xue Juzheng with the posthumous name Wenhui and Wang Pu with Wenxian—though recent precedent, are established custom.

sentences.zh: 若以臣父起家不由文學，即嘗歷集賢、修史之職，伏請改諡曰‘文’。”

translations.literal: "If because my father did not rise by literary studies, yet he once held posts in the Jixian Hall and in compiling history, I humbly request that the posthumous name be changed to Wen."
translations.idiomatic: If my father's rise was not through literary studies, he nevertheless once held posts in the Jixian Hall and in compiling history. I humbly request that his posthumous name be changed to Wen."

sentences.zh: 判太常禮儀院趙昂、判考功張洎駁曰：“沈倫逮事兩朝，早升台弼，有祗畏謹守之美，有矜恤周濟之心。

translations.literal: Zhao Ang of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Zhang Ji of the Board of Merit rebutted, saying: "Shen Lun served two dynasties and early rose to the chief minister's terrace; he had the beauty of reverent awe and careful preservation, and the heart of compassionate relief and all-round aid."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ang of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Zhang Ji of the Board of Merit rebutted, saying, "Shen Lun served two dynasties and rose early to chief minister. He showed reverent caution in office and a compassionate heart toward those in need.

sentences.zh: 案《諡法》：不懈於位，與夫謹事奉上、執事堅固、執禮御賓、率事以信、接下不驕、能遠恥辱、賢而不伐、尊賢貴讓、愛民長悌、不懈為德、既過能改，數者皆謂之‘恭’。

translations.literal: According to the Canon of Posthumous Names: not slack in office; together with reverently serving and upholding the sovereign, firm in conduct of affairs, upholding ritual in receiving guests, leading affairs with faith, receiving subordinates without arrogance, able to keep distant from shame and disgrace, worthy without boasting, honoring the worthy and valuing yielding, loving the people and long in fraternal duty, unslackening in virtue, and able to reform after fault—these several are all called Gong.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Canon of Posthumous Names, the following merit the name Gong: not slack in office; reverently serving the sovereign; firm in conduct; upholding ritual toward guests; leading affairs with faith; receiving subordinates without arrogance; keeping distant from shame; being worthy without boasting; honoring the worthy and valuing yielding; loving the people and long in fraternal duty; unslackening in virtue; and reforming after fault.

sentences.zh: 又云：慈民好與，與夫柔質慈民、愛民好柔、寬裕不苛、和質受諫，數者皆謂之‘惠’。

translations.literal: It also says: compassionate toward the people and fond of giving; together with gentle in nature and compassionate toward the people, loving the people and fond of gentleness, generous and not harsh, harmonious in nature and accepting remonstrance—these several are all called Hui.
translations.idiomatic: It also says that the name Hui applies to one who is compassionate toward the people and fond of giving; gentle in nature and compassionate toward the people; loving the people and fond of gentleness; generous and not harsh; and harmonious in nature and accepting remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 由漢以來，皆為美諡。

translations.literal: From Han onward these have all been fine posthumous names.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han onward these have all been honored posthumous names.

sentences.zh: 如唐相溫彥博之出納明允，止諡曰‘恭’；

translations.literal: For example the Tang chief minister Wen Yanbo, whose receipts and disbursements were clear and fair, received only the posthumous name Gong;
translations.idiomatic: For example the Tang chief minister Wen Yanbo, whose receipts and disbursements were clear and fair, received only the posthumous name Gong;

sentences.zh: 竇易直之公舉無避，乃諡曰‘恭惠’。

translations.literal: Dou Yizhi, whose public recommendations were without avoidance, received the posthumous name Gonghui.
translations.idiomatic: while Dou Yizhi, whose public recommendations were without favoritism, received Gonghui.

sentences.zh: 而沈倫備位台衡，出於際會，徒能謹飭以自保全，以‘恭’配‘惠’，厥美居多。

translations.literal: As for Shen Lun, he filled the chief minister's place and rose by timely chance; he could only be careful and restrained to preserve himself—pairing Gong with Hui, the beauties are mostly present.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Lun merely filled the chief minister's place and rose by timely chance. He could only be careful and restrained to preserve himself. Pairing Gong with Hui suits him well.

sentences.zh: 又按《諡法》：道德博聞曰‘文’，忠信接禮曰‘文’，寬不慢、廉不劌曰‘文’，堅強不暴曰 ‘文’，敏而好學、不恥下問曰‘文’，德美才秀曰‘文’，修治班製曰‘文’。

translations.literal: Again according to the Canon of Posthumous Names: broad in virtue and learning is called Wen; loyal and faithful in connecting with ritual is called Wen; broad without arrogance, incorrupt without harshness is called Wen; firm and strong without violence is called Wen; keen and fond of learning, not ashamed to ask those below is called Wen; virtue beautiful and talent outstanding is called Wen; repairing and ordering court ranks and regulations is called Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Again according to the Canon of Posthumous Names, Wen applies to one who is broad in virtue and learning; loyal and faithful in ritual conduct; broad without arrogance and incorrupt without harshness; firm and strong without violence; keen and fond of learning and not ashamed to ask those below; beautiful in virtue and outstanding in talent; or skilled in ordering court ranks and regulations.

sentences.zh: 昔張說之諡文正，楊綰之諡文簡，人不謂然。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhang Yue received the posthumous name Wenzheng and Yang Guan Wenzian—people did not consider this right.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Zhang Yue received the posthumous name Wenzheng and Yang Guan Wenzian, and people did not consider this justified.

sentences.zh: 蓋行義有所未充，雖蒙特賜，誠非至公。

translations.literal: This was because their conduct and righteousness had not been fully fulfilled; though they received the honored grant, it was truly not the utmost fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Their conduct and righteousness had not been fully fulfilled. Though they received the honored grant, it was not fully fair.

sentences.zh: 若夫大臣子孫，許其為父陳請，則曲臺、考功之司為虛器，而彰善癉惡之義微矣。

translations.literal: As for allowing a great minister's son to plead on his father's behalf, then the offices of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Board of Merit become empty vessels, and the meaning of displaying good and condemning evil grows faint.
translations.idiomatic: If great ministers' sons are allowed to plead on their fathers' behalf, the offices of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Board of Merit become empty formalities, and the purpose of displaying good and condemning evil is weakened.

sentences.zh: 繼宗以其父曾任集賢殿學士及監修國史之職，輒引薛居正、王溥為比，則彼皆奮跡辭場，曆典誥命，以‘文’為諡，允合國章。

translations.literal: Jizong, because his father once held the posts of academician of the Jixian Hall and supervisor of the national history, rashly cited Xue Juzheng and Wang Pu as comparisons—yet they both rose through effort in the literary arena and successively presided over edicts and commands; to take Wen as posthumous name truly accorded with national regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Jizong, because his father once held posts in the Jixian Hall and as supervisor of the national history, rashly cited Xue Juzheng and Wang Pu as comparisons. Yet they both rose through the literary arena and presided over edicts and commands. For them the posthumous name Wen accorded with national regulations.

sentences.zh: 至於集賢、國史，皆宰相兼領之任，非必由文雅而登。

translations.literal: As for the Jixian Hall and the national history, these are all posts concurrently held by chief ministers and need not be attained through literary refinement.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Jixian Hall and the national history, these are posts concurrently held by chief ministers and need not be attained through literary refinement.

sentences.zh: 其沈倫諡，伏望如故。

translations.literal: As for Shen Lun's posthumous name, I humbly hope it may remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: As for Shen Lun's posthumous name, I humbly hope it may remain as proposed.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court followed their recommendation.

sentences.zh: 子 繼宗

translations.literal: Son: Jizong
translations.idiomatic: Son: Jizong

sentences.zh: 繼宗，字世卿，倫為樞密副使，以蔭補西頭供奉官。

translations.literal: Jizong, courtesy name Shiqing, when Lun was vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs entered office by privilege as attendant of the western headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Jizong, courtesy name Shiqing, entered office by privilege as attendant of the western headquarters when his father was vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 倫作相，授水部員外郎，加朝散大夫。

translations.literal: When Lun became chief minister, Jizong was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Works and given the additional title of grand master of palace attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Lun became chief minister, Jizong was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Works and given the additional title of grand master of palace attendance.

sentences.zh: 遷都官、職方，知浚儀縣，轉屯田郎中，出知單州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministries of Justice and of Personnel, served as magistrate of Junyi county, was transferred to director in the Ministry of Public Works, and went out as prefect of Danzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Ministries of Justice and of Personnel, as magistrate of Junyi county, then as director in the Ministry of Public Works, and was sent out as prefect of Danzhou.

sentences.zh: 代歸，命使京東計度財賦。

translations.literal: When his replacement returned he was ordered on a mission to survey revenues in the eastern capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When his replacement arrived he was ordered to survey revenues in the eastern capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 濮州土貢銀，課民織造，不折省稅；

translations.literal: Puzhou's local tribute of silver required the people to weave and manufacture it, without deduction from provincial tax;
translations.idiomatic: In Puzhou the local tribute of silver required the people to weave and manufacture it without deduction from provincial tax;

sentences.zh: 鄆州節度配屬縣納藥物，皆為民病。

translations.literal: the Yanzhou military commission assigned subordinate counties to deliver medicines—all were hardships for the people.
translations.idiomatic: and the Yanzhou military commission assigned subordinate counties to deliver medicines—all burdens on the people.

sentences.zh: 繼宗歸，歷言於上以除其弊。

translations.literal: Jizong on his return fully reported these to the throne to abolish their abuses.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Jizong reported these abuses fully to the throne, which abolished them.

sentences.zh: 至道末，領淮南轉運使。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhidao he headed the Huainan transport commission.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhidao era he headed the Huainan transport commission.

sentences.zh: 繼宗貴家子，倦於從吏，既因疾，以將作少監致仕。

translations.literal: Jizong was the son of a noble house and weary of following official service; when illness came he retired as vice director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: Jizong, a son of a noble house, grew weary of official service. When illness came he retired as vice director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 東封歲，求扈從，復授職方郎中。

translations.literal: In the year of the eastern feng sacrifice he requested to accompany the entourage and was again appointed director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the year of the eastern feng sacrifice he asked to accompany the entourage and was again appointed director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，改太僕少卿、判吏部南曹，遷光祿少卿、判三司三勾院。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed he was changed to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and judge of the southern bureau of the Ministry of Personnel, then transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and judge of the Three Departments' three audit bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were completed he was made vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud with charge of the southern bureau of the Ministry of Personnel, then promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments with charge of the Three Departments' three audit bureaus.

sentences.zh: 繼宗善營產業，厚於養生，不飲酒，不嗜音律，而喜接賓客，終日宴集無倦。

translations.literal: Jizong was skilled at managing property, lavish in nurturing life, did not drink wine, did not love music, yet delighted in receiving guests and feasted all day without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Jizong was skilled at managing property and lavish in caring for his health. He did not drink wine or love music, yet delighted in entertaining guests and feasted all day without tiring.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符五年，卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died, at age fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 前後錄其子惟溫、惟清、惟恭，並為將作監主簿。

translations.literal: Earlier and later his sons Weiwen, Weiqing, and Weigong were recorded, all as chief clerks of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Weiwen, Weiqing, and Weigong were recorded in turn, all as chief clerks of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 惟溫後至秘書丞；

translations.literal: Weiwen later reached assistant director of the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Weiwen later rose to assistant director of the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 惟清娶密王女宜都縣主，至內殿承制。

translations.literal: Weiqing married the Princess of Yidu, daughter of Prince Mi, and reached drafter of the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqing married the Princess of Yidu, daughter of Prince Mi, and rose to drafter of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 盧多遜 父 億

translations.literal: Lu Duoxun; Father: Yi
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duoxun; Father: Yi

sentences.zh: 盧多遜，懷州河內人。

translations.literal: Lu Duoxun was a man of Henei in Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duoxun was a native of Henei in Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖得一、祖貞啟皆為邑宰。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Deyi and grandfather Zhenqi both served as district magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Deyi and grandfather Zhenqi both served as district magistrates.

sentences.zh: 父億，字子元，少篤學，以孝悌聞。

translations.literal: His father Yi, courtesy name Ziyuan, in youth devoted himself to learning and was known for filial piety and brotherly duty.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi, courtesy name Ziyuan, devoted himself to learning in youth and was known for filial piety and brotherly duty.

sentences.zh: 舉明經，調補新鄉主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the mingjing examination and was appointed to fill the post of chief clerk of Xinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the mingjing examination and was appointed chief clerk of Xinxiang.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，復試進士，校書郎、集賢校理。

translations.literal: When his term expired he again tested for jinshi and became collator and collating editor of the Jixian collection.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he again tested for the jinshi degree and became collator and collating editor of the Jixian collection.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，遷著作佐郎，出為鄆州觀察支使。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin he was transferred to assistant gentleman of the Secretariat and went out as investigating officer of the Yanzhou observation commission.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu era of the Later Jin he was promoted to assistant gentleman of the Secretariat and sent out as investigating officer of the Yanzhou observation commission.

sentences.zh: 節帥杜重威驕蹇黷貨，幕府賄賂公行，唯億清介自持。

translations.literal: The military commissioner Du Chongwei was arrogant, obstinate, and greedy; bribes ran openly in the headquarters, but Yi alone was pure and upright in self-restraint.
translations.idiomatic: The military commissioner Du Chongwei was arrogant, obstinate, and corrupt, and bribes ran openly through his staff, but Yi alone remained pure and upright.

sentences.zh: 會景延廣鎮天平，表億掌書記；

translations.literal: When Jing Yanguang governed Tianping he memorialized that Yi should head secretarial records;
translations.idiomatic: When Jing Yanguang governed Tianping he had Yi appointed head of secretarial records;

sentences.zh: 留守西洛，又表為判官。

translations.literal: when he remained to guard western Luo, he again memorialized to make Yi his judge.
translations.idiomatic: and when he remained to guard western Luo, he again had Yi appointed as his judge.

sentences.zh: 時國用窘乏，取民財以助軍，河南府計出二十萬緡，延廣欲並緣以圖羨利，增為三十七萬緡。

translations.literal: At the time state finances were strained and the people's wealth was taken to aid the army; Henan prefecture was assessed twenty thousand strings of cash; Yanguang wished to use the occasion to seek surplus profit and increased it to thirty-seven thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: State finances were then strained and wealth was taken from the people to aid the army. Henan prefecture was assessed twenty thousand strings of cash, but Yanguang sought surplus profit and increased the levy to thirty-seven thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 億諫曰：“公位兼將相，既富且貴。

translations.literal: Yi remonstrated, saying: "Your lordship's position combines general and minister; you are already rich and noble."
translations.idiomatic: Yi remonstrated, saying, "Your lordship holds both civil and military rank and are already rich and noble.

sentences.zh: 今國帑空竭，不得已而取貲於民，公何忍利之乎？

translations.literal: "Now the state treasury is empty and exhausted; we take funds from the people because we have no choice—how can your lordship bear to profit from it?"
translations.idiomatic: The state treasury is now empty and we take funds from the people only because we must. How can your lordship bear to profit from it?

sentences.zh: ”延廣慚而止。

translations.literal: Yanguang, ashamed, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang, ashamed, desisted.

sentences.zh: 漢初，以魏王承訓為開封尹，授億水部員外郎，充推官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, when Prince Wei Chengchun was prefect of Kaifeng, Yi was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Works and served as investigator.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Later Han, when Prince Wei Chengchun was prefect of Kaifeng, Yi was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Works and served as investigator.

sentences.zh: 時侍衛諸軍驕恣，朝廷姑息之，軍士成美以驢負鹽入都門，閽者不敢執，反擒平民孟柔送侍衛司。

translations.literal: At the time the various armies of the personal guard were arrogant and willful, and the court indulged them. The soldier Cheng Mei entered the capital gate with salt loaded on a donkey; the gatekeepers dared not arrest him but instead seized the commoner Meng Rou and sent him to the guard command.
translations.idiomatic: The personal guard armies were then arrogant and willful, and the court indulged them. A soldier named Cheng Mei entered the capital gate with salt loaded on a donkey. The gatekeepers dared not arrest him but instead seized a commoner named Meng Rou and sent him to the guard command.

sentences.zh: 柔自誣伏，論當棄市。

translations.literal: Rou falsely confessed; by judgment he should be executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Rou falsely confessed and was sentenced to execution in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 億察其冤，言於漢祖而釋之。

translations.literal: Yi perceived his injustice, spoke to the Han founder, and had him released.
translations.idiomatic: Yi perceived the injustice, spoke to the Han founder, and had him released.

sentences.zh: 周初，為侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou he became attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Later Zhou he became attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 漢末兵亂，法書亡失。

translations.literal: At the end of Han military chaos caused the legal texts to be lost.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Later Han military chaos had caused the legal texts to be lost.

sentences.zh: 至是，大理奏重寫律令格式，統類編敕。

translations.literal: By this time the Court of Judicial Review memorialized to rewrite the codes, statutes, formats, and unified categories of compiled edicts.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Court of Judicial Review memorialized to rewrite the codes, statutes, formats, and compiled edicts in unified categories.

sentences.zh: 乃詔億與刑部員外郎曹匪躬、大理正段濤同加議定。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Yi together with Cao Feigong, vice director in the Ministry of Justice, and Duan Tao, director of the Court of Judicial Review, jointly to deliberate and fix them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered Yi, together with Cao Feigong, vice director in the Ministry of Justice, and Duan Tao, director of the Court of Judicial Review, to deliberate and fix them jointly.

sentences.zh: 舊本以京兆府改同五府，開封、大名府改同河南府，長安、萬年改為次赤縣，開封、浚儀、大名、元城改為赤縣。

translations.literal: The old text changed Jingzhao prefecture to rank with the five prefectures, Kaifeng and Daming prefectures to rank with Henan prefecture, Chang'an and Wannian to secondary red counties, and Kaifeng, Junyi, Daming, and Yuancheng to red counties.
translations.idiomatic: The old text changed Jingzhao prefecture to rank with the five prefectures, Kaifeng and Daming to rank with Henan prefecture, Chang'an and Wannian to secondary red counties, and Kaifeng, Junyi, Daming, and Yuancheng to red counties.

sentences.zh: 又定東京諸門薰風等為京城門，明德等為皇城門，啟運等為宮城門，升龍等為宮門，崇元等為殿門。

translations.literal: They also fixed the eastern capital's gates: Xunfeng and others as capital city gates, Mingde and others as imperial city gates, Qiyun and others as palace city gates, Shenglong and others as palace gates, Chongyuan and others as hall gates.
translations.idiomatic: They also designated the eastern capital's gates: Xunfeng and others as capital city gates, Mingde and others as imperial city gates, Qiyun and others as palace city gates, Shenglong and others as palace gates, and Chongyuan and others as hall gates.

sentences.zh: 廟諱書不成文，凡改點畫及義理之誤字二百一十有四。

translations.literal: Taboo characters for the temple were written without forming complete text; altogether they changed two hundred fourteen mistaken characters in strokes and in meaning and principle.
translations.idiomatic: Taboo characters for the imperial temple were written without forming complete text. Altogether they corrected two hundred fourteen mistaken characters in strokes or meaning.

sentences.zh: 又以晉、漢及周初事關刑法敕條者，分為二卷，附編敕，自為《大周續編敕》，詔行之。

translations.literal: They also took matters from Jin, Han, and early Zhou relating to penal law and edict articles, divided them into two juan, appended them to the compiled edicts, and made them separately into the Continued Compiled Edicts of Great Zhou; an edict put this into effect.
translations.idiomatic: They also collected matters from the Later Jin, Later Han, and early Zhou relating to penal law and edict articles, divided them into two juan, and issued them separately as the Continued Compiled Edicts of Great Zhou, which an edict put into effect.

sentences.zh: 俄以本官知雜事，加左司員外郎，遷主客度支郎中，並兼弘文館直學士。

translations.literal: Soon with his existing office he handled miscellaneous matters, was given the additional title of vice director in the left bureau, was transferred to director in the Ministries of Rites and Revenue, and concurrently held academician directly attached to the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he handled miscellaneous matters in his existing office, was given the additional title of vice director in the left bureau, was promoted to director in the Ministries of Rites and Revenue, and concurrently served as academician directly attached to the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 世宗晏駕，為山陵判官，出為河南令。

translations.literal: When Shizong died he served as judge for the imperial tomb and went out as magistrate of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong died he served as judge for the imperial tomb and was sent out as magistrate of Henan.

sentences.zh: 宋初，遷少尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was transferred to vice prefect.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song he was promoted to vice prefect.

sentences.zh: 億性恬退，聞其子多遜知制誥，即上章求解。

translations.literal: Yi's nature was calm and retiring; when he heard that his son Duoxun had become drafter of edicts, he at once submitted a memorial requesting release from office.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was calm and retiring by nature. When he heard that his son Duoxun had become drafter of edicts, he at once submitted a memorial requesting release from office.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，以少府監致仕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande he retired as director of the Palace Domestic Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiande he retired as director of the Palace Domestic Office.

sentences.zh: 多遜，顯德初，舉進士，解褐秘書郎、集賢校理，遷左拾遺、集賢殿修撰。

translations.literal: Duoxun, at the beginning of Xiande, passed the jinshi examination, left the russet robe as secretary, collating editor of the Jixian collection, was transferred to left remonstrance-reminder and compiler of the Jixian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Duoxun passed the jinshi examination in the early Xiande era, entered office as secretary and collating editor of the Jixian collection, and was promoted to left remonstrance-reminder and compiler of the Jixian Hall.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，以本官知制誥，歷祠部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong, with his existing office he became drafter of edicts and successively served as vice director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianlong he became drafter of edicts while retaining his existing rank and served successively as vice director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，權知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande he was given provisional charge of the civil-service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiande he was given provisional charge of the civil-service examinations.

sentences.zh: 三年，加兵部郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year he was given the additional title of director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was given the additional title of director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 四年，復權知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again had provisional charge of the civil-service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he again had provisional charge of the civil-service examinations.

sentences.zh: 六年，加史館修撰、判館事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was given the additional titles of compiler of the History Office and judge of the office's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was given the additional titles of compiler of the History Office and placed in charge of its affairs.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，車駕征太原，以多遜知太原行府事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao, when the imperial carriage campaigned against Taiyuan, Duoxun was made to manage the traveling headquarters at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao, when the emperor campaigned against Taiyuan, Duoxun was placed in charge of the traveling headquarters there.

sentences.zh: 移幸常山，又命權知鎮州。

translations.literal: When the court moved to favor Changshan, he was again ordered to have provisional charge of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved to Changshan, he was again given provisional charge of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 師還，直學士院。

translations.literal: When the army returned he served directly in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he served directly in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 三年春，復知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he again had charge of the civil-service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he again had charge of the civil-service examinations.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，命為翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year he was appointed Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year he was appointed Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 六年，使江南還，因言江南衰弱可圖之狀。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, returning from a mission to Jiangnan, he reported the condition of Jiangnan's weakness and how it could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, returning from a mission to Jiangnan, he reported how weak Jiangnan had become and how it might be conquered.

sentences.zh: 受詔同修《五代史》，遷中書舍人、參知政事。

translations.literal: He received an edict to compile jointly the History of the Five Dynasties, was transferred to secretariat drafter, and became participant in governance.
translations.idiomatic: He received an edict to compile jointly the History of the Five Dynasties, was promoted to secretariat drafter, and became participant in governance.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱，數日起復視事。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his father; after several days he was recalled from mourning to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his father and was recalled from mourning to resume office after only a few days.

sentences.zh: 會史館修撰扈蒙請復修時政記，詔多遜專其事。

translations.literal: At this time History Office compiler Hu Meng requested restoration of compiling the Records of Current Administration; an edict put Duoxun solely in charge of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Hu Meng, compiler of the History Office, requested that the Records of Current Administration be resumed, and an edict put Duoxun solely in charge of the work.

sentences.zh: 金陵平，加吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Jinling was pacified, he was given the additional title of vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinling was pacified, he was given the additional title of vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，拜中書侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he received appointment as vice director of the Secretariat and grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taiping Xingguo era he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 四年，從平太原還，加兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, returning from pacifying Taiyuan, he was given the additional title of minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, returning from the pacification of Taiyuan, he was given the additional title of minister of war.

sentences.zh: 多遜博涉經史，聰明強力，文辭敏給，好任數，有謀略，發多奇中。

translations.literal: Duoxun was broadly versed in the classics and histories, intelligent and forceful, quick and fluent in literary expression, fond of stratagems, possessed of strategy, and many of his schemes proved uncannily effective.
translations.idiomatic: Duoxun was broadly versed in the classics and histories, intelligent and forceful, quick and fluent in writing, fond of stratagems and skilled in planning, and many of his schemes proved uncannily effective.

sentences.zh: 太祖好讀書，每取書史館，多遜預戒吏令白己，知所取書，必通夕閱覽，及太祖問書中事，多遜應答無滯，同列皆伏焉。

translations.literal: Taizu loved reading; whenever he sent for books from the History Office, Duoxun beforehand instructed the clerks to inform him and tell him which books were requested; he would read them through the night, and when Taizu questioned him on matters in the books, Duoxun answered without hesitation; his colleagues all submitted to him in respect.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu loved reading. Whenever he sent for books from the History Office, Duoxun had the clerks notify him in advance of which volumes were requested; he would then read them straight through the night. When Taizu questioned him about their contents, Duoxun answered without hesitation, and his colleagues all stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 先是，多遜知制誥，與趙普不協，及在翰林日，每召對，多攻普之短。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Duoxun was drafter of edicts, he was at odds with Zhao Pu; when in the Hanlin Academy, each time he was summoned for audience he often attacked Pu's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while serving as drafter of edicts, Duoxun had been at odds with Zhao Pu; during his days in the Hanlin Academy, whenever he was summoned for audience he often attacked Pu's shortcomings.

sentences.zh: 未幾，普出鎮河陽。

translations.literal: Before long Pu went out to command Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Pu was sent out to serve as military governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 太宗踐祚，普入為少保。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded to the throne, Pu entered court as Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong ascended the throne, Pu was recalled to court as Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 數年，普子承宗娶燕國長公主女，承宗適知潭州，受詔歸闕成婚禮。

translations.literal: Several years later, Pu's son Chengzong married the daughter of the Princess of Yan; Chengzong happened to be prefect of Tanzhou and received an edict to return to the capital for the wedding.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, Pu's son Chengzong married the daughter of the Princess of Yan. Chengzong was then serving as prefect of Tanzhou and received an edict to return to the capital for the wedding ceremony.

sentences.zh: 未逾月，多遜白遣歸任，普由是憤怒。

translations.literal: Before a month had passed, Duoxun reported to have him sent back to his post; Pu was therefore enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Before a month had passed, Duoxun memorialized to have him sent back to his post, and Pu was enraged by this.

sentences.zh: 初，普出鎮河陽，上言自訴云：“外人謂臣輕議皇弟開封尹，皇弟忠孝全德，豈有間然。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Pu went out to command Heyang, he submitted a memorial in self-defense saying: "Outsiders say that Your subject lightly discussed the emperor's younger brother, prefect of Kaifeng. The emperor's younger brother is wholly loyal and filial in virtue—how could there be any breach?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Pu was sent out to command Heyang, he submitted a memorial in self-defense stating: "Outsiders claim that I spoke lightly of the emperor's younger brother, the Prefect of Kaifeng. The emperor's younger brother is utterly loyal and filial in every way—how could there be any breach between us?"

sentences.zh: 矧昭憲皇太后大漸之際，臣實預聞顧命。

translations.literal: Moreover, as Empress Dowager Zhaoxian was critically ill, Your subject was in fact present to hear the final testament.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when Empress Dowager Zhaoxian was near death, I was in fact present to hear the final testament.

sentences.zh: 知臣者君，願賜昭鑒。

translations.literal: He who knows his subject is his ruler; I beg that clear discernment be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Only the ruler truly knows his subject's heart; I beg that Your Majesty grant me clear discernment.

sentences.zh: ”太祖手封其書，藏於宮中。

translations.literal: Taizu personally sealed his memorial and stored it in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu personally sealed the memorial and stored it in the palace.

sentences.zh: 至是，普復密奏：“臣開國舊臣，為權幸所沮。

translations.literal: At this point Pu again submitted a secret memorial: "Your subject is an old minister from the founding of the state and has been obstructed by favorites."
translations.idiomatic: At this point Pu submitted another secret memorial: "I am an old minister from the founding of the state and have been obstructed by favorites at court."

sentences.zh: ”因言昭憲顧命及先朝自訴之事。

translations.literal: He then spoke of Empress Dowager Zhaoxian's final testament and his earlier self-defense at the previous court.
translations.idiomatic: He then spoke of Empress Dowager Zhaoxian's final testament and his earlier memorial of self-defense at Taizu's court.

sentences.zh: 上於宮中訪得普前所上表，因感悟，即留承宗京師。

translations.literal: The emperor searched in the palace and found Pu's earlier memorial; moved by this, he at once kept Chengzong in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor searched the palace archives and found Pu's earlier memorial; moved by this, he at once retained Chengzong in the capital.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復用普為相，多遜益不自安。

translations.literal: Before long Pu was again employed as chief minister; Duoxun grew ever more ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Pu was restored as chief minister, and Duoxun grew increasingly uneasy.
