translations.literal: Qi again submitted a memorial on border affairs, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Qi submitted another memorial on border affairs, saying:

sentences.zh: “臣頃任延州節度判官，經涉五年，雖未嘗躬造夷落，然常令蕃落將和斷公事，歲無虛月，蕃部之事，熟於聞聽。

translations.literal: "Your subject recently served as administrative aide of the Yanzhou military commission for five years; though I never personally visited the barbarian settlements, I regularly had tribal leaders mediate official business—month after month without fail—and am well acquainted through hearing of tribal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: "Your subject recently served as administrative aide of the Yanzhou military commission for five years. Though I never personally visited the barbarian settlements, I regularly had tribal leaders mediate official business, month after month without fail, and am well acquainted with tribal affairs through what I have heard.

sentences.zh: 大約党項、吐蕃風俗相類，其帳族有生戶、熟戶，接連漢界、入州城者謂之熟戶，居深山僻遠、橫過寇略者謂之生戶。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, Tangut and Tibetan customs are similar. Their clans divide into raw and tame households: those connected to the Han border who enter prefectural cities are called tame households; those dwelling in deep mountains and remote places who cross over to raid are called raw households.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, Tangut and Tibetan customs are similar. Their clans divide into raw and tame households: those living along the Han border who enter prefectural cities are called tame households, while those dwelling in deep mountains and remote places who cross over to raid are called raw households.

sentences.zh: 其俗多有世仇，不相來往，遇有戰鬥，則同惡相濟，傳箭相率，其從如流。

translations.literal: Their custom involves many hereditary feuds—they do not visit one another. When fighting occurs, those who share enmity assist each other; they pass arrows to summon followers, and compliance flows like water.
translations.idiomatic: Their custom involves many hereditary feuds, and they do not visit one another. When fighting breaks out, those who share a grudge assist each other; they pass arrows to summon followers, and men follow as if carried by a stream.

sentences.zh: 雖各有鞍甲，而無魁首統攝，並皆散漫山川，居常不以為患。

translations.literal: Though each has saddle and armor, there is no chief to command and gather them; all are scattered across mountains and rivers and ordinarily do not pose a threat.
translations.idiomatic: Though each man has saddle and armor, there is no chief to command and gather them. All are scattered across mountains and rivers and ordinarily pose no threat.

sentences.zh: 党項界東自河西銀、夏，西至靈、鹽，南距鄜、延，北連豐、會。

translations.literal: The Tangut frontier runs east from Yin and Xia in Hexi, west to Ling and Yan, south to Fu and Yan, and north connecting Feng and Hui.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut frontier runs east from Yin and Xia in Hexi, west to Ling and Yan, south to Fu and Yan, and north to Feng and Hui.

sentences.zh: 厥土多荒隙，是前漢呼韓邪所處河南之地，幅員千里。

translations.literal: That land has much waste and open space—it is the Henan region where Han-era Huhanxie lived, a thousand li square.
translations.idiomatic: That land has much waste and open space. It is the Henan region where Huhanxie of the Former Han lived, a thousand li square.

sentences.zh: 從銀夏至青、白兩池，地惟沙磧，俗謂平夏；

translations.literal: From Yinxia to the Green and White salt pools, the ground is only sand and gravel—they call it Pingxia;
translations.idiomatic: From Yinxia to the Green and White salt pools, the ground is only sand and gravel. Colloquially this is called Pingxia;

sentences.zh: 拓拔，蓋蕃姓也。

translations.literal: Tuoba—that is a barbarian surname.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba—that is a barbarian surname.

sentences.zh: 自鄜、延以北，多土山柏林，謂之南山；

translations.literal: North of Fu and Yan prefectures, there are many earthen hills and cypress forests—they call it the Southern Mountains;
translations.idiomatic: North of Fu and Yan prefectures there are many earthen hills and cypress forests, called the Southern Mountains;

sentences.zh: 野利，蓋羌族之號也。

translations.literal: Yeli—that is the name of a Qiang tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Yeli—that is the name of a Qiang tribe.

sentences.zh: 從延州入平夏有三路：一、東北自豐林縣葦子驛至延川縣接綏州，入夏州界；

translations.literal: From Yan Prefecture into Pingxia there are three routes: one, northeast from Fenglin County's Weizi Post Station to Yanchuan County connecting Suizhou, entering Xia Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: From Yan Prefecture into Pingxia there are three routes. One runs northeast from Weizi Post Station in Fenglin County to Yanchuan County, connecting with Suizhou and entering Xia Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 一、正北從金明縣入蕃界，至盧關四五百里，方入平夏州南界；

translations.literal: one, due north from Jinming County into barbarian territory, four or five hundred li to Lu Pass before entering southern Pingxia;
translations.idiomatic: one runs due north from Jinming County into barbarian territory, four or five hundred li to Lu Pass before entering southern Pingxia;

sentences.zh: 一、西北歷萬安鎮經永安城，出洪門至宥州四五百里，是夏州西境。

translations.literal: one, northwest through Wan'an garrison and Yong'an city, out Hong Gate to You Prefecture four or five hundred li—that is the western border of Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: one runs northwest through Wan'an garrison and Yong'an city, out Hong Gate to You Prefecture four or five hundred li away—that is the western border of Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 我師如入夏州之境，宜先招致接界熟戶，使為向導，其強壯有馬者，令去官軍三五十里踏白先行。

translations.literal: If our army enters Xia Prefecture territory, it should first summon tame border households as guides; those strong and with horses should be sent thirty to fifty li ahead of the army to clear the path.
translations.idiomatic: If our army enters Xia Prefecture territory, it should first summon tame border households as guides. Those who are strong and have horses should be sent thirty to fifty li ahead of the army to clear the path.

sentences.zh: 緣此三路，土山柏林，溪谷相接，而復隘狹不得成列，躡此鄉導，可使步卒多持弓弩槍鋸隨之，以三二千人登山偵邏，俟見坦途寧靜，可傳號勾馬遵路而行，我皆嚴備，保無虞也。

translations.literal: Along these three routes—earthen hills, cypress forests, streams and ravines connecting yet narrow and cramped so formations cannot be drawn up—following these local guides, infantry can carry many bows, crossbows, spears, and saws; two or three thousand men climb hills to scout; when they see open calm road, signal and bring cavalry along the route; we stay fully prepared and will be safe.
translations.idiomatic: Along these three routes, earthen hills and cypress forests give way to streams and ravines that connect yet remain narrow and cramped, so formations cannot be drawn up. Following these local guides, infantry can carry many bows, crossbows, spears, and saws, while two or three thousand men climb the hills to scout. When they see open, calm road, signal and bring the cavalry along the route. If we stay fully prepared, we will be safe.

sentences.zh: 長興四年，夏州李仁福死，有男彝超擅稱留後。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changxing, Li Renfu of Xia Prefecture died; his son Yichao seized the title of acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Changxing, Li Renfu of Xia Prefecture died. His son Yichao seized the title of acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 當時詔延州安從進與李彝超換鎮，彝超據夏州，固不奉詔，朝廷命邠州藥彥稠總兵五萬送從進赴任。

translations.literal: At the time the court ordered Yanzhou's An Congjin to exchange posts with Li Yichao; Yichao held Xia Prefecture and firmly refused the edict; the court commanded Binzhou's Yao Yanchou with fifty thousand troops to escort Congjin to his post.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court ordered An Congjin of Yan Prefecture to exchange posts with Li Yichao. Yichao held Xia Prefecture and refused the edict. The court commanded Yao Yanchou of Bin Prefecture to lead fifty thousand troops to escort Congjin to his post.

sentences.zh: 時頓兵城下，議欲攻取，軍儲不繼，遽命班師。

translations.literal: At the time they halted below the city; some proposed attack, but army stores could not keep up and they suddenly ordered withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the army halted below the city. Some proposed an attack, but army stores could not keep up, and they suddenly ordered withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 而振旅之時，不能嚴整，失戈棄甲，遂為邊人之利。

translations.literal: At the time of re-forming ranks they could not maintain discipline; spears and armor were abandoned, and this became profit for border people.
translations.idiomatic: When the army re-formed ranks it could not maintain discipline. Spears and armor were abandoned, and the border people profited from the disorder.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞党項號為小蕃，非是敵，若得出山布陣，止勞一戰，便可蕩除。

translations.literal: Your subject also hears that the Tangut are called a small barbarian—not a match for us; if they come out of the mountains to deploy formations, one battle would suffice to wipe them out.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject also hears that the Tangut are called a minor barbarian people and are no match for us. If they come out of the mountains to deploy in formation, one battle would suffice to wipe them out.

sentences.zh: 深入則饋運艱難，窮追則窟穴幽隱，莫若緣邊州鎮，分屯重兵，俟其入界侵漁，方可隨時掩擊，非為養勇，亦足安邊。

translations.literal: Deep advance makes supply difficult; hot pursuit finds hidden lairs—better to station heavy forces at border prefectures and garrisons; when they cross to plunder, strike opportunely—not to hoard martial spirit but to secure the border.
translations.idiomatic: Deep advance makes supply difficult, and hot pursuit leads only to hidden lairs. Better to station heavy forces at border prefectures and garrisons, and when they cross the frontier to plunder, strike at the opportune moment. This is not merely to hoard martial spirit—it is enough to secure the border.

sentences.zh: 凡烏合之徒，勢不能久，利於速鬥，以騁兵鋒。

translations.literal: All rabble gathered cannot endure long; they favor quick fights to show their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Rabble gathered in haste cannot endure long. They favor quick fights to show their martial edge.

sentences.zh: 莫若持重守疆，以挫其銳。

translations.literal: Better to hold weighty defense of the frontier and blunt their sharpness.
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold the frontier with weighty defense and blunt their sharpness.

sentences.zh: 彼無城守，眾乏餱糧，威賞不行，部族分散，然後密令覘其保聚之處，預於麟、府、鄜、延、寧、慶、靈、武等州約期會兵，四面齊進，絕其奔走之路，合勢擊之，可以剪除無噍類矣。

translations.literal: They have no walled towns, lack rations, rewards and punishments fail, clans scatter—then secretly watch where they gather; pre-arrange allied troops from Lin, Fu, Fu, Yan, Ning, Qing, Ling, and Wuzhou prefectures, advance from four sides, cut escape routes, combine forces—the whole lot can be exterminated without survivors.
translations.idiomatic: They have no walled towns, lack rations, and rewards and punishments fail, so their clans scatter. Then secretly watch where they gather, pre-arrange allied troops from Lin, Fu, Fu, Yan, Ning, Qing, Ling, and Wuzhou prefectures, advance from four sides, cut off their escape routes, and combine forces to strike. The whole lot can be exterminated without survivors.

sentences.zh: 仍先告諭諸軍，擊賊所獲生口、資畜，許為己有，彼為利誘，則人百其勇也。

translations.literal: Also first announce to all armies that captives and livestock taken from fighting the enemy may be kept as their own—with profit as lure, each man will be a hundred times braver.
translations.idiomatic: Also announce beforehand to all armies that captives and livestock taken from fighting the enemy may be kept as their own. With profit as lure, each man will fight a hundred times harder.

sentences.zh: 靈武路自通遠軍入青岡峽五百里，皆蕃部熟戶。

translations.literal: The Lingwu route from Tongyuan Army through Qinggang Gorge five hundred li—all tame tribal households.
translations.idiomatic: The Lingwu route from Tongyuan Army through Qinggang Gorge for five hundred li is all tame tribal households.

sentences.zh: 向來使人、商旅經由，並在部族安泊，所求賂遺無幾，謂之“打當 ”，亦如漢界逆旅之家宿食之直也。

translations.literal: Envoys and merchants passing through always lodged with tribes; bribes sought were few—they call it "da dang," like inn charges for lodging and food on the Han frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys and merchants passing through always lodged with the tribes. The bribes sought were few—they call it "da dang," like the charges at inns for lodging and food on the Han frontier.

sentences.zh: 此時大軍或須入其境，則向導踏白，當如夏州之法。

translations.literal: When a great army must enter their territory, guides and path-clearers should follow the Xia Prefecture method.
translations.idiomatic: When a great army must enter their territory, guides and path-clearers should follow the Xia Prefecture method.

sentences.zh: 況彼靈州便是吾土，芻粟儲畜，率皆有備。

translations.literal: Moreover Ling Prefecture is our soil; fodder, grain, and stored livestock are generally all prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Ling Prefecture is our own territory. Fodder, grain, and stored livestock are generally all prepared.

sentences.zh: 緣路五七程，不煩供饋，止令逐都兵騎，裹糧輕齎，便可足用。

translations.literal: Five to seven stages along the route need not trouble supply—have each command's cavalry carry grain lightly and that suffices.
translations.idiomatic: For five to seven stages along the route there is no need to trouble supply lines. Have each command's cavalry carry grain lightly and that will suffice.

sentences.zh: 諺所謂“磨鐮殺馬”，劫一時之力也，旬浹之餘，固無闕乏矣。

translations.literal: As the proverb says, "grind the scythe to slaughter the horse"—exertion for a moment; after ten-plus days there will be no shortage.
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb says, "grind the scythe to slaughter the horse"—it is exertion for a moment. After ten-plus days there will be no shortage.

sentences.zh: 又臣曾受任西川數年，經歷江山，備見形勢要害。

translations.literal: Your subject also once served in western Sichuan for several years, traversing rivers and mountains, fully seeing terrain and key points.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject also once served in western Sichuan for several years, traversing rivers and mountains and seeing firsthand the terrain and key points.

sentences.zh: 利州最是咽喉之地。

translations.literal: Lizhou is the throat position above all.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhou is above all the throat of the region.

sentences.zh: 西過桔柏江，去劍門百里，東南去閬州，水陸二百餘里，西北通白水、清川，是龍州入川大路，鄧艾於此破蜀，至今廟貌存焉。

translations.literal: West past Jubei River, a hundred li from Jian Gate; southeast two hundred-plus li by water and land to Lang Prefecture; northwest connects Bait and Qingchuan—it is the great road from Long Prefecture into Sichuan; Deng Ai here broke Shu; temple images remain to this day.
translations.idiomatic: West of it lies the Jubei River, a hundred li from Jian Gate. Southeast it is two hundred-plus li by water and land to Lang Prefecture. Northwest it connects Bait and Qingchuan. This is the great road from Long Prefecture into Sichuan. Deng Ai broke Shu here, and a temple still stands to this day.

sentences.zh: 其外三泉、西縣，興、鳳等州，並為要衝，請選有武略重臣鎮守之。”

translations.literal: Beyond it, Sanquan, Xi County, Xing, Feng, and other prefectures are all key crossings—please select able military ministers to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond it, Sanquan, Xi County, Xing, Feng, and other prefectures are all key crossings. Please select able military ministers to garrison them.

sentences.zh: 奏入，上密寫其奏，令繼隆擇利而行。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor personally copied it and had Jilong act as profit dictated.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor personally copied it and had Jilong act as opportunity allowed.

sentences.zh: 至道元年春，大宴於含光殿，上問琪年，對曰：“七十有九。

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of Zhidao, a great banquet was held at Hanguang Hall; the emperor asked Qi's age; he replied: "Seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the first year of Zhidao, a great banquet was held at Hanguang Hall. The emperor asked Qi's age, and he replied, "Seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: ”上因慰撫久之。

translations.literal: " The emperor therefore consoled him at length.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor therefore consoled him at length.

sentences.zh: 二年春，拜右僕射，特令月給實奉一百千，又以其衰老，詔許五日一朝。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year he was appointed Right Vice Director; specially granted a monthly stipend of one hundred thousand cash; and because of his age, permitted court audience every five days.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the second year he was appointed Right Vice Director, granted a special monthly stipend of one hundred thousand cash, and because of his advanced age was permitted to attend court once every five days.

sentences.zh: 是年九月被病，令其子貽序秉筆，授辭作《多幸老民敘》，大抵謂《洪範》五福，人所難全，而己兼有之，實天幸也。

translations.literal: That year in the ninth month he fell ill; he had his son Yixu hold the brush and dictated words to compose An Account of a Greatly Fortunate Old Commoner, broadly saying that the five blessings in the Great Plan from the Book of Documents are hard for anyone to possess fully, yet he had them all—it was truly heaven's fortune.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the ninth month he fell ill. He had his son Yixu hold the brush and dictated An Account of a Greatly Fortunate Old Commoner, saying in essence that the five blessings set forth in the Great Plan from the Book of Documents are hard for anyone to possess fully, yet he had them all—a true gift of heaven.

sentences.zh: 又口占遺表數百字而卒。

translations.literal: He also orally composed a final memorial of several hundred characters and died.
translations.idiomatic: He also orally composed a final memorial of several hundred characters and died.

sentences.zh: 贈司空，諡惠安。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Minister of Works; posthumous name Huian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Works, with the posthumous name Huian.

sentences.zh: 起復貽序為右讚善大夫，貽庥為大理評事，貽廣童子出身。

translations.literal: Yixu was recalled from mourning as right aide to the heir apparent; Yixiu as case reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review; Yiguang entered through youth examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yixu was recalled from mourning as right aide to the heir apparent, Yixiu as case reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review, and Yiguang entered service through the youth examination.

sentences.zh: 貽序上表乞終喪制，從之。

translations.literal: Yixu submitted a memorial begging to complete mourning observances; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yixu submitted a memorial requesting to complete the mourning period, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，錄其孫宗諒試秘書郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxi, his grandson Zongliang was tried as secretary gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianxi era, his grandson Zongliang was appointed probationary secretary gentleman.

sentences.zh: 琪素有文學，頗諧捷。

translations.literal: Qi was always literary and quite quick-witted.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had always been literary and was quite quick-witted.

sentences.zh: 在使府前後三十年，周知人情，尤通吏術。

translations.literal: At commissioner offices for thirty years altogether, he thoroughly knew human affairs and was especially skilled in administrative methods.
translations.idiomatic: He served at commissioner offices for thirty years altogether, knew human affairs thoroughly, and was especially skilled in administrative methods.

sentences.zh: 在相位日，百執事有所求請，多面折之，以是取怨於人。

translations.literal: During his days as chief minister, when officials requested things he often rebuked them to their face—thus earning resentment from others.
translations.idiomatic: During his days as chief minister, when officials came with requests he often rebuked them to their face, and for this earned resentment.

sentences.zh: 貽序嘗預修《冊府元龜》，筆劄遒勁。

translations.literal: Yixu once participated in compiling the Prime Tortoise of the Book Repository; his writing was vigorous.
translations.idiomatic: Yixu once participated in compiling the Prime Tortoise of the Book Repository, and his writing was vigorous.

sentences.zh: 未幾，坐事左遷復州副使，起為殿中丞卒。

translations.literal: Before long, because of an offense he was demoted to vice commissioner of Fu Prefecture; recalled as palace secretary and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was demoted for an offense to vice commissioner of Fu Prefecture. He was later recalled as palace secretary and died in office.

sentences.zh: 宋雄者，亦幽州人。

translations.literal: Song Xiong was also a man of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Song Xiong was also a native of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 初與琪齊名燕、薊間，謂之“二宋”。

translations.literal: Initially he was equally famous with Qi in Yan and Ji—they were called "the Two Songs."
translations.idiomatic: In his early years he was as famous as Qi throughout Yan and Ji, and the two were called "the Two Songs."

sentences.zh: 雄仕契丹為應州從事。

translations.literal: Xiong served the Khitan as staff member of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong served the Khitan as a staff member of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，王師北伐，雄與其節度副使艾正以城降，授正本州觀察使，以雄為鴻臚少卿同知州事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, when the imperial army marched north, Xiong and the military vice commissioner Ai Zheng surrendered the city; Ai Zheng was made observation commissioner of the prefecture, and Xiong was made Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations and co-administrator of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi, when the imperial army marched north, Xiong and the military vice commissioner Ai Zheng surrendered the city. Ai Zheng was made observation commissioner of the prefecture, and Xiong was made Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations and co-administrator of prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 改光祿少卿，歷知均、唐二州。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and successively governed Jun and Tang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and successively governed Jun and Tang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 未幾，護河陰屯兵，以知河渠利害，因命領護汴口，均節水勢，以達轉漕，京師賴之。

translations.literal: Before long he guarded the Yellow River garrison; knowing the advantages and disadvantages of canals and sluices, he was therefore ordered to oversee Bian mouth, regulate water flow to enable transport, and the capital relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was put in charge of the Yellow River garrison. Knowing the advantages and disadvantages of canals and sluices, he was ordered to oversee Bian mouth and regulate the water flow to enable transport. The capital relied on him.

sentences.zh: 改太子詹事，復為光祿少卿，遷將作監。

translations.literal: He was changed to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, again made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and promoted to Director of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, again made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and promoted to Director of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 所至職務修舉，公私倚任焉。

translations.literal: Wherever he went duties were well performed, and public and private alike relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went his duties were well performed, and both public and private affairs relied on him.

sentences.zh: 雄涉獵文史，善談論，有氣節，士流多推許之。

translations.literal: Xiong ranged broadly in literature and history, was good at discussion, had integrity, and men of the gentry greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong ranged broadly in literature and history, was skilled in discussion, and had integrity. Men of the gentry greatly praised him.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde he died, at age seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingde he died at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 錄其子可久為太常寺奉禮郎，賦祿終制。

translations.literal: His son Kejiu was enrolled as ceremonial attendant of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, with salary through the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kejiu was enrolled as ceremonial attendant of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, with salary granted through the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自薛居正而下，嘗居相位者凡四人，其始終出處雖不同，然觀於其行事，概可見矣。

translations.literal: Discussion: From Xue Juzheng downward, those who once held the chief minister's post number four in all. Their beginnings and ends, rise and withdrawal, differ, yet viewed in their conduct, the outline may be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Discussion: From Xue Juzheng downward, four men once held the chief minister's post. Their beginnings and ends, rise and withdrawal, differ, yet viewed in their conduct, the outline may be seen.

sentences.zh: 初，朗州亡卒嘯聚為盜，監軍使疑城中僧千餘人皆與謀，欲盡殺之，居正緩其事，賊禽而僧不與，卒賴以活。

translations.literal: At first, discharged soldiers in Lang Prefecture gathered with a war cry as bandits; the military supervisor suspected that more than a thousand monks in the city were all in the plot and wished to kill them all. Juzheng delayed the matter; the bandits were captured and the monks had no part—in the end they were preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: At first, discharged soldiers in Lang Prefecture gathered as bandits. The military supervisor suspected that more than a thousand monks in the city were all in the plot and wished to kill them all. Juzheng delayed the matter. The bandits were captured, and the monks had taken no part—in the end they were spared.

sentences.zh: 沈倫使吳越還，請以揚、泗軍儲百萬餘斛貸饑民，朝論難之。

translations.literal: Shen Lun, returning from a mission to Wuyue, requested that more than a million hu of military stores from Yang and Si be lent to starving people; court discussion opposed it.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Lun, returning from a mission to Wuyue, requested that more than a million hu of military stores from Yang and Si be lent to starving people. Court discussion opposed it.

sentences.zh: 倫曰：“國家以廩粟濟民，自當召和氣，致豐稔，豈復有水旱？

translations.literal: Lun said: "When the state uses granary grain to aid the people, it should naturally summon harmonious qi and bring abundant harvest—how could there again be flood and drought?
translations.idiomatic: Lun said, "When the state uses granary grain to aid the people, it should naturally summon harmonious qi and bring abundant harvests. How could flood and drought return?

sentences.zh: ”得請乃已。

translations.literal: " He obtained permission and only then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " He obtained permission and only then stopped.

sentences.zh: 太祖每取書史館，盧多遜預戒吏令白己，知所取，必通夕閱覽，以是答問多中。

translations.literal: Whenever Taizu sent for books from the History Office, Lu Duoxun beforehand instructed the clerks to inform him and tell him which books were requested; he would read them through the night, and by this his answers in questioning mostly hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Taizu sent for books from the History Office, Lu Duoxun had the clerks notify him in advance of which volumes were requested. He would read them straight through the night, and by this his answers in questioning mostly hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 宋琪始為程羽、賈琰所抑，繼為多遜所忌，其後自員外郎歲中四遷至尚書，居相位。

translations.literal: Song Qi was first held down by Cheng Yu and Jia Yan, then envied by Duoxun; afterward, from outer-section director he was promoted four times within a year to minister, and held the chief minister's post.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qi was first held back by Cheng Yu and Jia Yan, then envied by Duoxun. Afterward, from outer-section director he was promoted four times within a year to minister and reached the chief minister's post.

sentences.zh: 即此而觀，則守道蒙福者非幸致，而投荒竄死者非不幸也。

translations.literal: Viewed from this, those who keep to the Way and receive blessing do not attain it by luck, and those who are cast into exile and die in flight are not unfortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Viewed from this, those who keep to the Way and receive its reward do not attain it by luck, and those cast into exile to die in flight are not simply unfortunate.

sentences.zh: 宋雄善持論，有氣節，雖與琪齊名，而爵位不侔者，所遇不同焉爾。

translations.literal: Song Xiong was good at holding to argument and had integrity; though equally famous with Qi, his rank did not match—what they encountered differed, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Song Xiong was skilled in debate and had integrity. Though equally famous with Qi, his rank did not match—what they encountered differed, that is all.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，自昔懷材抱藝，而抑鬱下僚以終其身者多矣，豈特宋雄為然哉！

translations.literal: Alas, from old those who cherished talent and held skill yet ended their lives depressed in low office have been many—was Song Xiong alone in this!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, from old there have been many who cherished talent and held skill yet ended their lives in low office, frustrated and unrewarded. Was Song Xiong alone in this!
